text: As the audience thinned. <break time="0.8s" /> The chase led us at last. <break time="0.8s" /> Into the most noisome quarter of London. <break time="0.8s" /> Where everything bore the worst impress. <break time="0.8s" /> Of deplorable poverty and of desperate crime. <break time="0.8s" /> Here the old man brightened up. <break time="0.8s" /> Like a lamp nearly burnt out. <break time="0.8s" /> That suddenly flares again. <break time="0.8s" /> And he strode once more. <break time="0.8s" /> With an elastic step. <break time="0.8s" /> Among the wretched figures. <break time="0.8s" /> Still roaming the lanes. <break time="0.8s" /> Near daybreak. <break time="0.8s" /> We reached one of the huge suburban temples of Intemperance. <break time="0.8s" /> And with a half shriek of joy. <break time="0.8s" /> The old man forced his way in resuming at once his aimless pacing. <break time="0.8s" /> Among the throng. <break time="0.8s" /> Before long, however. <break time="0.8s" /> A rush to the door showed. <break time="0.8s" /> That the host was closing up for the night. <break time="0.8s" /> And the look upon the old mans face. <break time="0.8s" /> At that moment. <break time="0.8s" /> Was more intense than despair itself. <break time="0.8s" /> Yet he did not hesitate in his career. <break time="0.8s" /> But with a mad energy. <break time="0.8s" /> Retraced his steps at once. <break time="0.8s" /> To the heart of mighty London. <break time="0.8s" /> Where all day long. <break time="0.8s" /> He wandered to and fro amid the turmoil. <break time="0.8s" /> As the shades of the second evening came on I grew wearied unto death. <break time="0.8s" /> And stopping fully in front of the wanderer. <break time="0.8s" /> I gazed at him steadfastly in the face. <break time="0.8s" /> Yet he did not notice me. <break time="0.8s" /> This old man. <break time="0.8s" /> I said at length. <break time="0.8s" /> Is the type and the genius of deep crime. <break time="0.8s" /> He refuses to be alone. <break time="0.8s" /> And he is the man of the crowd. <break time="0.8s" /> It will be in vain to follow. <break time="0.8s" /> For I shall learn no more of him. <break time="0.8s" /> And perhaps it is but one. <break time="0.8s" /> Of the great mercies of God. <break time="0.8s" /> That the worst heart of the world. <break time="0.8s" /> Does not permit itself to be read.
